name: NY-11
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by about 10 points on the partisan baseline
Malliotakis holds a massive financial advantage, over $2.7 million cash on hand versus roughly $35,000 for DeCillis
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 93 percent
No public polling of the general election
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Malliotakis: a Republican-leaning district, incumbency, and an overwhelming fundraising edge, with markets pricing her near certain to win. With no polls and no expert ratings, uncertainty stays moderate but the expected margin remains around fifteen points Republican.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much closer race or a major outside-spending intervention for DeCillis would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Nicole Malliotakis seeks a third term in a Staten Island–based district that voted about ten points more Republican than the nation in recent cycles. She enters the general election with roughly $2.8 million raised and $2.8 million on hand, while Democrat Michael DeCillis has raised under $70,000 and has no meaningful outside support. No public polls of the race are available, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets give the Republican about a 93 percent chance of holding the seat. The forecast expects Malliotakis to win by roughly fifteen points, consistent with the district's lean plus her incumbency and financial advantages, though the absence of polling keeps some uncertainty in the estimate.
